oneLiner: Outlook email and Teams stalled worldwide for nearly a full day.
whatYouSaw: Work emails wouldn't send, Teams chats froze, and logins failed across businesses, hospitals (including UK NHS trusts), and government offices.
why: A hidden software mistake—sitting quietly since a July update—woke up on Microsoft's main network gateways when heavy traffic shifted during lower capacity. Microsoft confirmed it was not a cyberattack.
analogy: Like a highway tollbooth lane having a stuck gate all summer that nobody noticed until rush-hour traffic got rerouted through that exact lane.
technical: A dormant Windows networking defect on Exchange Online gateway servers triggered under shifted traffic load and reduced capacity, cascading into Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for ~23h 50m.

oneLiner: A local power disruption in London slowed UK banking and retail apps for 6 hours.
whatYouSaw: Several UK banking apps and websites hosted in London felt sluggish or briefly failed to load overnight and into Tuesday morning.
why: An outside electrical power interruption struck one London building. Traffic automatically shifted to neighboring London buildings, which briefly caused traffic jams while absorbing the extra crowd.
analogy: Like one terminal at a busy airport losing power: flights move to the next terminal so travel keeps going, but security lines get crowded until the lights come back on.
technical: An external electrical power disruption impacted Google Cloud zone europe-west2-b; failover traffic created transient latency and elevated errors across europe-west2 for 6 hours and 8 minutes.

oneLiner: A routine security list accidentally doubled in size and stalled major websites for ~3 hours.
whatYouSaw: People across the world hit sudden error pages on major news sites, shops, and everyday web apps.
why: A routine internal database change caused an automated list of bad-bot rules to duplicate itself. When that oversized list reached Cloudflare's front-door servers, it exceeded a safety size limit and crashed them.
analogy: Like a printer glitch doubling a restaurant menu to 400 pages—so every waiter's clipboard snapped the moment they picked it up.
technical: A ClickHouse permissions change duplicated entries in a Bot Management feature file beyond a hard-coded limit in Cloudflare's core proxy software, causing global 5xx errors.

oneLiner: A glitch in Northern Virginia rippled across popular North American apps.
whatYouSaw: Popular apps, smart-home devices, and online checkouts across North America froze or refused to connect early Monday morning.
why: An internal health-checking and address-lookup glitch inside Amazon's oldest and busiest East Coast hub triggered a domino effect across services that relied on it.
analogy: Like the main air-traffic radar at a hub airport mistakenly marking healthy runways closed—delaying dozens of airlines that connect through that city.
technical: Centered in AWS US-EAST-1 (N. Virginia), a malfunction in internal Network Load Balancer health monitoring and DNS automation cascaded across EC2 and DynamoDB-dependent workloads.
